name: Kempinski Palace Engelberg
positioning: Alpine hotel in the centre of the Swiss mountain village of Engelberg, beside the Kurpark and a short walk from the cableways
best_for: Skiers and hikers who want to walk to the cableways from the village centre
Families who want a certified Kids Club and rooms that sleep four

facts.text: Engelberg is reached by the Zentralbahn railway from Zurich or Lucerne, and the train station is 100 metres from the hotel.
The Titlis cable car station is 600 metres from the hotel.
Engelberg Abbey is 500 metres from the hotel.
The aerial cableways into the mountains are a few minutes' walk from the hotel.
The Ladies in Red make sure birthdays, anniversaries and other occasions are celebrated in style.
Some room categories, including the Premier Room, Junior Suite, Titlis Suite, Belle Epoque Suite and Park Suite, accommodate up to four guests, and connecting rooms are possible.
The spa has a pool area, a sauna area and a fitness centre.
Dining venues include Cattani, the Palace Bar and in-room dining, with vegetarian and vegan dishes across all of them.
Ski tickets and day or week passes can be bought at the hotel's reception desk.
Hotel guests can buy TITLIS Tower tickets at reception at a preferential rate, including the return cable car to Titlis and the Horizon Deck.
The hotel's Golf Fun Package arranges the green fee and tee time at the 18-hole Engelberg-Titlis golf course.
Children play in the Kids Club without electronic devices.

highlights.text: For more than a decade every guest has been welcomed by the hotel's Lady in Red, a host dressed in red who offers help and local knowledge.
The hotel is right next to the Kurpark, in the middle of Engelberg's village centre with its small shops, cafes and monastery.
The Kids Club is certified by the Luxury Childcare Association.
Intersport Achermann has an in-house shop renting ski, snowboard, cross-country, hiking and bike equipment.
The Activity Concierge puts together programmes, arranges cable car tickets and a hiking guide, and can show guests the region himself on an e-bike.

considerations.text: Snow and ice are common on the roads in the canton of Obwalden, especially in winter, and the hotel strongly recommends winter equipment for cars.
Dogs are welcome only in some areas of the hotel, for a nightly fee.
WhataHotel notes premium luxury pricing reflecting the exclusive mountain resort positioning.
